note: Teach-the-craft carousels. Same design system, light cover always, diagram-forward interiors. See ideas/README.md for the design direction and feed rules. `needsStack:true` means the topic asserts something about Kymbo's own tooling — verify against stack.json before writing copy.

pillars.The Stack: What the tools are and how they connect.
pillars.The Build: How a thing actually gets made, step by step.
pillars.The Standard: What 'good' means technically, with a number attached.
pillars.The Fix: A specific failure, its cause, and the repair.
pillars.The Tradeoff: Two valid options and how to choose.

coverRule: surface is ALWAYS light. These are the tiles that fill the feed's light slots.

topics.title: The five layers of a hotel tech stack
topics.hook: Your hotel runs on 5 systems. Most owners can only name 2.
topics.angle: Name the layers, then show that the booking engine is the only one that decides who owns the guest.
proof: PMS · channel manager · booking engine · payments · CRM
hub-and-spoke: the PMS is the hub

topics.title: Hub and spoke: why the PMS sits in the middle
topics.hook: Every integration you'll ever buy plugs into one box.
topics.angle: Diagram the spoke pattern — it explains why 'does it integrate with my PMS' is the only question that matters when buying anything.
proof: 5 primary integrations radiate from the PMS

topics.title: What happens between 'Book now' and your inbox
topics.hook: Nine things happen in the 3 seconds after a guest hits Book.
topics.angle: Walk the request lifecycle: availability check → hold → payment authorization → PMS write → channel push → confirmation. Demystifies the product Kymbo sells.
proof: auth vs capture are two different moments

topics.title: Two-way vs one-way sync (this is how double bookings happen)
topics.hook: One-way sync tells the OTA nothing. That's the bug.
topics.angle: The single most expensive misconfiguration in small-property tech, explained in one diagram.
proof: proper channel manager integration drops overbookings by 90%+
iCal sync is often one-way by default

topics.title: Widget or full build — how to choose
topics.hook: You don't always need a new website.
topics.angle: Decision tree, not a sales pitch: when a widget on the existing site genuinely wins, and the three conditions that force a full build.
proof: Path 01 widget vs Path 02 full build

topics.title: WordPress vs headless: who owns your SEO output
topics.hook: Going headless silently breaks your schema. Here's why.
topics.angle: The real distinction isn't speed, it's which system emits the canonical, the sitemap and the JSON-LD. Strong, genuinely non-obvious.
proof: WordPress owns content fields; Next.js owns URL, metadata, canonical, JSON-LD, sitemap, redirects
a headless migration is where schema breaks silently

topics.title: The 5 schema types every hotel site needs
topics.hook: Schema is how AI search learns your hotel exists.
topics.angle: Very timely: JSON-LD is now the input for AI Overviews and chat-search citations, not just rich snippets.
proof: Hotel · LocalBusiness · AggregateRating · Offer · FAQPage
JSON-LD is Google's recommended format
most hospitality sites implement one type or none

topics.title: Your site takes 6.3 seconds. Google wants 2.5.
topics.hook: The average hotel page loads in 6.3s. The bar is 2.5s.
topics.angle: Lead with the industry-average gap — it lands harder than generic 'speed matters' advice.
proof: average hotel page load 6.3s vs 2.5s 'Good' LCP
53% of mobile visitors abandon after 3s
1s delay ≈ 7% fewer conversions

topics.title: LCP, INP, CLS — explained without the jargon
topics.hook: Three letters decide whether Google shows your hotel.
topics.angle: Define each by what the guest actually feels, then attach the threshold. INP matters most for a booking engine — date pickers are interaction-heavy.
proof: LCP < 2.5s
INP < 200ms
INP above 300ms → 34% lower completion rate

topics.title: The image pipeline that costs you bookings
topics.hook: Your room photos are the reason the page is slow.
topics.angle: Hotels are photo-heavy by nature, so this is the highest-leverage speed fix for this specific audience. WebP/AVIF, srcset, lazy-loading below the fold, never lazy-load the hero.
proof: WebP compression + edge CDN + script deferral → up to 28% more direct conversions

topics.title: Google free booking links: zero commission, most hotels miss it
topics.hook: There's a free slot on Google labelled 'Official site'.
topics.angle: Genuinely actionable and under-used by independents. Explain the connectivity-partner requirement — that's the part that stops people.
proof: clicks are free
needs a connectivity partner sending live rates + availability
listed as 'Official site' under All options

topics.title: OTA, metasearch, direct — three different money models
topics.hook: Three ways a guest arrives. Three completely different bills.
topics.angle: Commission vs CPC vs free. Most owners treat all traffic as one thing; the pricing model is the whole story.
proof: metasearch CPC or commission-per-stay
free booking links 0

topics.title: Gateway, processor, merchant account — who's who
topics.hook: Three companies touch every card payment. You're paying all three.
topics.angle: Nobody explains this cleanly to small operators, and it's where hidden per-booking cost lives.
proof: authorization vs capture
a connected gateway improves authorization rates and simplifies reconciliation

topics.title: PCI basics for a property taking cards
topics.hook: If you email a card number, you own the breach.
topics.angle: Scope reduction is the lesson: use a hosted/tokenized field and your PCI burden collapses. Concrete and slightly scary — good retention.
proof: tokenization keeps card data out of your systems

topics.title: What a channel manager does when you change one rate
topics.hook: You change €10. Watch what fires.
topics.angle: Trace one edit across every connected surface. Makes an invisible system visible — perfect diagram carousel.
proof: 30% less manual OTA management within a quarter

topics.title: Domain, DNS, hosting, CDN — the four people confuse
topics.hook: Your domain is not your hosting. This costs people weeks.
topics.angle: Foundational, evergreen, and the reason migrations go wrong. Frame as four boxes and who you pay for each.

topics.title: A booking form without HTTPS is a dead form
topics.hook: One browser warning ends the booking.
topics.angle: Short, absolute, easy to verify — pairs well as a quick-hit carousel between heavier ones.

topics.title: The 5-step mobile booking flow that converts
topics.hook: Dates. Rooms. Rate. Summary. Details. Nothing else.
topics.angle: Directly mirrors the flow in our own demo product — the carousel doubles as a product demo without being an ad.
proof: every extra step is an abandonment opportunity

topics.title: How abandoned-booking recovery actually fires
topics.hook: They left at the payment step. You have about an hour.
topics.angle: Explain the trigger mechanics — the event, the delay window, the consent requirement. Most people think it's magic.

topics.title: GDPR for guest data, in five plain rules
topics.hook: You collected the email. Now you're responsible for it.
topics.angle: Consent, purpose limitation, retention, access, deletion — applied to a hotel CRM specifically. Unsexy, high-trust, very shareable with owners.

topics.title: The GA4 events that actually measure a booking funnel
topics.hook: Pageviews tell you nothing. Six events tell you everything.
topics.angle: Name the events and where each fires in the flow. Turns analytics from decoration into diagnosis.
proof: search → view_item → begin_checkout → add_payment_info → purchase

topics.title: How to read your booking engine's conversion rate
topics.hook: 2% doesn't mean anything until you know the denominator.
topics.angle: Sessions vs searches vs availability-found — three denominators, three wildly different numbers, and vendors quote whichever flatters them.

topics.title: Staging, backups, uptime — the boring stuff that saves you
topics.hook: The worst time to learn you have no backup is Friday.
topics.angle: Frame as three cheap insurances with the cost of skipping each. Good candidate for a QUOTE-layout interior.

topics.title: Anatomy of a booking page that converts
topics.hook: Nine elements. Miss three and the page leaks.
topics.angle: Labelled teardown of a real page — our own demo product, annotated. Strong device-composite candidate.
